title.en: Somebody's Mother (poem): kindness to the old

text.en: An old woman stands alone at a busy crossing, afraid to cross, while schoolboys pass by playing and laughing.

The poem tells about an old woman standing at a crossing for a long time, hesitant to cross the busy road.
A group of schoolboys pass by, playing and laughing, and most of them hurry past.
One boy stops, takes the woman's hand and helps her to the other side.
The boy returns to his friends feeling proud of what he did, and the poem shows how a small act of kindness matters.
The poet shows the woman's helplessness through her age, her waiting alone and her fear of the traffic.
The poem's title reminds us that every old person is somebody's mother, and we should treat everyone with respect.
The word ragged here means old and torn like shabby clothes.
The poem has a regular rhyme and tells a story, so it is a narrative poem.
The message is that empathy, understanding another's feelings, leads us to help.
We can show kindness today by helping the old, the sick and those who are alone.
